subject: gzip and rmr, setting the correct input format

messages.author: e0fda2e7aa5c3e59
messages.subject: gzip and rmr, setting the correct input format
parts:
Hello,

I am looking for any pointers or guidance on the make.input.format function.  I am attempting to read a gzip file in the map phase and attempting to use the make.input.format to setup the input correctly for mapreduce.  I am using -D options we use for Java Streaming, namely:

-D mapred.output.compression.codec=org.apache.hadoop.io.compress.GzipCode \

-D mapred.output.compress=true \

Here is my sample code.  When I run this, I never get the stderr output and I quickly get a "Error: Java heap space" in the console.  The file I am reading is fairly large.

Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/usr/local/bin/hadoop")
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_STREAMING="/usr/local/Cellar/hadoop/2.5.0/libexec/share/hadoop/tools/lib/hadoop-streaming-2.5.0.jar")

library(rhdfs)
hdfs.init() 
library(rmr2)

json_reducer <- function(name, counts) {
  keyval(name, sum(counts))}

json_mapper <- function(k, v)
{
  write(paste("Running Mapper"), stderr())
  keyval("test", 1)
}

custInput <- make.input.format(format = "native", mode = "binary", backend.parameters = 
                                 list(D="mapred.input.compression.codec=org.apache.hadoop.io.compress.GzipCode",
                                      D="mapred.output.compress=true")) 

from.dfs(
  mapreduce(
    input = "/user/brohoro/gziptest/myfile.gz",
    input.format = custInput,
    map = json_mapper,
    combine = T, # use the reduce function as the combiner
    reduce = json_reducer)
)

I took a look the thread here (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/rhadoop/gzip/rhadoop/XgnhJkcGgbs/syggsPq4QZEJ) but am unable to replicate the success here. 

I can successful view the contents of the file in hadoop using something like:

hadoop fs -text /user/brohoro/gziptest/myfile.gz | head

Any assistance would be appreciated.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1704] gzip and rmr, setting the correct input format
parts:
Hi Brian,
have you tried help(make.input.format)? First, you don't tell us what the format of your data is, besides that it is compressed.  I will assume json from the function names you are using. I see a couple of problems with your use of that function. If you specify format as a string, you are calling from predefined combination of the other options. It's the quick-and-easy. If you want full flexibility, you have to specify format as a function, then mode, streaming format and optionally backend parameters. Mix the two and you won't get what you expect. The other thing, native is not json.  I suspect you are sending json into the parser for typedbytes which is not the most resilient component ever written. That's probably where you get the heap space problem. We support json-ish with make.input.format("json"), but I call it json-ish because we need to have one json object per line and to have newlines and tabs escaped. That's how we made json fit with what hadoop streaming expects (on record per line, key and value separated by the first tab). So if you have any json that won't work. It's not the ideal level of json support, we accept suggestions on how to make it better. The missing piece is a json parser that can read one object from a connection. Right now we need to read x lines from stdin and pass them to the parser, which fails if the json object is not complete, hence the decision to put an object per line. Most people will need to preprocess their json before using this input, which is less than ideal. If you wanted to write your own input format, I would go about it as follows

true.json.format.fun = function(con){
 text = readLines(con, n = ...)
 obj = parse.json(text)
 keyval(NULL, obj)}

This is a function taking a connection as input and returning a key-val pair. What I don't know is the value for n or how to parse a partial json obj. Maybe you can make additional assumptions for your application, maybe you have a parser that can read from a connection or can develop one. Then you assemble the input format

true.json.input.format = make.input.format(format = true.json.format.fun, mode = "text", backend.parameters = <as you have them already>)


It would be nice to have a general json reader and replace the json-ish one we have now. Pull requests welcome.


Antonio

messages.author: e0fda2e7aa5c3e59
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1704] gzip and rmr, setting the correct input format
parts:
Antonio,

Thank you for the thoughtful reply!  The files are block compressed sequence files where records are written as text but do contain JSON.  I switched back to using mapred.LocalJobRunner and the following input type:

custInput <- make.input.format(format = "sequence.typedbytes")

This allowed me to process a 900k record file successfully. My original problem was compounded by a configuration problem with R in our dev cluster that was causing the “"Error: Java heap space" message regardless of the input type used.

Brian
